approach.method_basis: The Parent is a population-based molecular optimizer with a learned second proposal source. It keeps the 64 best molecules it has actually had scored, draws breeding parents from fixed score quantiles, and builds a surplus field of 160 fresh candidates for every announced batch of ten. Three quarters of that field come from the inherited graph generator: about two attempts in five recombine a connected fragment of two scored parents, the rest apply one to three successive single-atom or single-bond edits to one parent, with longer walks only when the local neighbourhood keeps rejecting. The remaining quarter is written by a small autoregressive SMILES model trained once, during preparation, on the supplied unlabeled molecule corpus and then frozen and objective-blind: for such a slot the same parent draw picks a scored molecule, its serialization is cut in half, and the model writes a new ending for it, so one proposal can rebuild a ring system and several atoms at once. Earlier children added the surrounding guards that both origins pass: direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, every product must pass a stable canonical identity check and two duplicate scopes, and a narrow admission gate rejects any product that introduces a sulfur environment outside a fixed neutral envelope relative to its own scored parents. Which ten of the 160 candidates are actually evaluated is decided by a Gaussian process fitted only to this session's accepted scores over integer-count Morgan fingerprints with a generalized Tanimoto covariance, through ten correlated draws from its joint posterior. The measured consequence is that the sequence model's distant proposals are offered to that surrogate exactly as they are decoded, are priced below the graph-edit group almost always, and are bought about one time in twenty.
approach.novelty: Finish the distant proposal before anyone prices it. When the sequence model's product has passed the inherited graph, identity, duplicate and sulfur checks, four single-edit variants of that product are made with the same graph operators the optimizer already uses, at their unchanged probabilities, and are put through the same checks; the surrogate the search has already fitted for this batch is then asked, once, for the predicted score of the decoded product and of its admissible variants, and the best-predicted member takes the slot. No oracle call, no second model, no extra model fit, no change to what gets evaluated, and nothing at all happens on graph-origin slots. This is the first mechanism on this lineage that does work between generating a candidate and offering it: the three earlier proposal-source children changed where larger moves come from (local-context fragment substitution, fragment-typed crossover, a physicochemical niche recipe) and lost, the round-39 to round-42 family changed how many, how wide, how often or from which generator, and the one earlier arm that queried the same predicted score inside the generator did so on the graph-edit path the surrogate already favoured, choosing between two fresh edits of an intermediate instead of polishing a far-away product that the surrogate systematically down-prices. The complementary arm planned in parallel on this same Parent forces the allocator to buy the raw distant chemistry; this one leaves the allocator alone and changes the chemistry so that an unchanged allocator would want it. Both the thing it must buy and the thing it must not lose are registered in advance: the price of prior-origin members has to rise, and their distance from the conditioning parent has to survive, or the arm has merely become an expensive graph-edit path.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-d527b3b4e2cb solved the supply problem and stopped one stage later: a distant prior-origin proposal is priced and evaluated exactly as it is decoded, and nothing finishes it. Its receipts are unambiguous. Supply activated as registered (17,302 of 69,600 admitted pool members prior-origin, realized share 0.2486, every session at or above 0.231, 98 of 17,400 slots taking the twelve-attempt graph fallback) and the chemistry really is different (median count-Morgan Tanimoto to the conditioning parent 0.6092 against the graph arm's 0.8326 in the same sessions, 82.7% at or below 0.70 against 24.0%, median heavy-atom change four against one, Murcko core changed 97.2% against 69.8%), while the graph arm stayed on the Anchor's own reference. What failed is the arrival point: prior-origin members were priced below the graph-edit group in 433 of 435 batches with the gap widening 0.0257 / 0.1155 / 0.1498 across session thirds, the unchanged correlated Thompson draw bought 231 of 4,350 evaluations (5.31%) and nothing at all in 292 of 435 batches, the picks it did make were uncertainty draws (in-pool uncertainty percentile 0.780 against predicted-score percentile 0.415), and conversion failed on its own terms - accepted median score 0.1853 against the graph arm's 0.2891, parent-beat 0.108 against 0.148, survivor rate 0.675 against 0.796, mean child-minus-best-parent -0.0682, 13 incumbent improvements carrying 0.1405 of the node's 5.0403 realized increment mass (2.8%), and not one of the 231 in any session's highest-scoring thirty molecules. The molecular review of the same node reads it the same way and names the missing stage: the continuations are farther and more makeable (median synthetic accessibility 2.4-4.1 against 3.0-5.2) but land off the incumbent's scoring ridge and are then evaluated raw, so a generator that wants both would have to refine them with local edits seeded on the continuation before they are scored. Against the Anchor n-1744a1494180 the Parent's panel is 0.5445 (-0.0519 paired), outside the ungated law-free band of n-1c2f17550a3e (-0.009888; band [-0.050871, +0.031095]). The behaviour that limits the Parent is therefore one specific thing: between decoding a distant continuation and pricing it, the Parent performs no work at all.

literature_review.conclusion: The search found no paper that tests this stage under these constraints - a bounded, oracle-free local refinement of whole-sequence proposals screened by the very accepted-only Gaussian process that will later price them, inside a 300-observation budget with a frozen objective-blind prior. The two closest sources support the design's direction without supplying it: MIMOSA establishes that screening a few bounded local edits with an available learned model is a workable way to improve a molecule, and the self-improvement work confirms that surrogate distribution shift against out-of-distribution candidates is a recognized failure, which is what this Parent measured. Both remedies in the literature require oracle-labelled or online-updated models that this profile forbids, so the adoption basis stays internal evidence with empty adoptions, and the arm is pre-registered on the Parent's own measured ranges.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The intervention and every number in it are derived from this campaign's own receipts, not from a paper: the Parent's per-origin pricing (prior group below the graph group in 433 of 435 batches, gap widening 0.0257 / 0.1155 / 0.1498), its purchase rate (231 of 4,350; 292 of 435 batches buying none), its conversion (accepted median 0.1853 against 0.2891, parent-beat 0.108, 2.8% of increment mass), its structural receipts (median Tanimoto 0.6092, 70.3% changing three or more heavy atoms, 97.2% core change) and the molecular review's prescription of local edits seeded on the continuation. The design parameters are fixed by the frozen ticket (k=4, the already-fitted posterior mean as the statistic, prior-origin slots only) and by the inherited code (operator families and probabilities, admission path, pool target), and the cost argument uses the Parent's own timings. No external setting, weight or asset is borrowed.
queries: surrogate-guided local refinement of generated molecules before oracle evaluation sample-efficient molecular optimization pre-screening
MIMOSA multi-constraint molecule sampling GNN-guided local edits MCMC molecular optimization

sources.applicability: Independent precedent that screening a small set of bounded local edits with an already-available model is a sensible way to move a molecule, which is the shape of this stage; it supplies no parameter here, because its weights come from dedicated pretrained networks and an MCMC target, while this arm reuses the search's own accepted-only posterior mean once per slot and spends no oracle call.
sources.finding: Starts from an input molecule and repeatedly proposes add/replace/delete local edits with property-agnostic pretrained graph networks, attaching a weight to each candidate edit and selecting promising candidates by those weights before the next iteration, rather than evaluating every edit.
sources.title: MIMOSA: Multi-constraint Molecule Sampling for Molecule Optimization

sources.applicability: Names, in the literature, the exact failure this Parent measured - an accepted-only kernel regressing unfamiliar candidates toward the archive mean and down-pricing them - and supports treating the generator/surrogate handoff as the lever. Its remedy is a jointly trained generative-predictive model with online updates, which this profile forbids (300 accepted observations per task, a frozen objective-blind prior and no gradient update online), so nothing is adopted from it.
sources.finding: Reports that surrogate property models used inside molecular optimization suffer distribution shift as the search drives candidates increasingly out of distribution, and keeps generation aligned with the surrogate to mitigate it.
sources.title: Sample Efficient Generative Molecular Optimization with Joint Self-Improvement

hypothesis: Insert one bounded, oracle-free refinement stage between admission and pooling, for prior-origin slots only. When a decoded prior continuation has passed the inherited admission path (checked_molecule, pool_identity_admission, the emitted/initial and temporary-pool duplicate scopes, and the sulfur introduction audit against its single conditioning parent), exactly k=4 single-call variants of that admitted molecule are generated with the inherited GraphOperators.mutate at its unchanged operator names and probabilities and its unchanged internal retry behaviour, and each variant is passed through exactly the same inherited admission path against the same conditioning parent. The admitted continuation and its admissible variants - at most five molecules - are then scored in one query of the posterior already fitted for this announced batch, through the selector's existing features/distribution interface, and the member with the greatest posterior mean fills the slot; a tie or no improvement keeps the raw continuation, so the occupant is never worse-predicted than the decoded product. No oracle call, no additional posterior fit, no new covariance factorization, no new asset and no new dependency is added, the selector's own random generator is never consumed, and the refinement draws its operator randomness from a dedicated stream seeded from the session seed so the inherited generator's stream is not spent on it. Everything else is the inherited node: the frozen corpus prior and its per-seed checkpoint, prefix rule, temperature and twelve attempts per slot; the slot rule index mod 4 == 3 with the inherited graph fallback, so the realized prior-origin share stays at its registered quarter; the three-quarter graph-edit path with its crossover, floor-one continuation law and rejection-conditioned escalation; the pool target of 160; the accepted-only count-Morgan Gaussian process with its kernel, normalization, noise, jitter ladder and finite guards; and the correlated Thompson allocation with its availability masks and tie rules. One k=4 and one screening statistic are bound; no sweep of k, of the operator mixture or of the statistic follows this arm.

finding_summary.headline: Refinement ran on every prior slot and kept its distance; panel +0.046 vs the Parent, but 38% is one deco_hop cell bought on exploration
finding_summary.insights:
The round-42 question is now answered in its two halves, and they separate cleanly. A bounded, oracle-free local refinement can be made to run at full coverage on this Parent at negligible cost and without surrendering the distance that made the prior interesting - that was the real risk and it did not happen, so "polishing destroys the distance" is ruled out for this operator family at k=4. But the refinement does not move prior-origin chemistry onto the incumbent scoring ridge: the accepted median score of its products went down, not up, and the surrogate still prices the group near the 0.46 percentile with unchanged uncertainty. The off-ridge explanation of the round-42 failure survives as an explanation and is not removed by this remedy, and pricing is not what admits these candidates: the one cell that carries the gain was bought on uncertainty, at a below-median predicted percentile, which is the allocator exploring and not the screen persuading.

The reason the screen cannot do more is measurable and it is a property of the statistic, not of k. Across the 201 selected variant-occupied picks, the larger the posterior-mean gain the refinement claimed, the further realized score fell below prediction (correlation -0.39), and the variant-occupied picks' predictive RMSE on this group rose from 0.0843 to 0.1102 while within-batch rank quality stayed where it was (Spearman about 0.52-0.60, unchanged from the Parent). Choosing the best of five by the mean of an accepted-only similarity-kernel posterior is a winner's curse: it selects the member whose optimism is largest, which is the member most similar to what has already scored, so a screen meant to finish a distant proposal instead domesticates it by a few thousandths. The molecular review independently reaches the same place from the chemistry: the winning edit was a single-atom move in 9,830 of the 12,181 replacements against 1,998 ring moves and 353 bond-order changes, so refinement re-decorates a molecule and never repairs or rebuilds a ring system or installs a whole functional group - and the one breakthrough edit installed an N-F bond onto an N-Cl nitrogen, a motif a chemist would reject, on a benchmark that does not price it out.

What this makes worth trying is therefore a change of statistic and of granularity, not a change of k or of the operator mix. The screening statistic needs to be something other than the same posterior mean the selector is about to maximize - predicted improvement, an uncertainty-aware or novelty-adjusted criterion, or a chemistry-side acceptance rule independent of the surrogate - and the variants need moves at fragment or ring-system granularity so one accepted refinement step can complete a structure. A valence-and-stability filter in the shared admission path would also change what both origins can reach the top with. The trajectories add a method-level diagnosis that no parameter will fix: late search collapses onto one decorated framework (9-58% of proposals in the last hundred evaluations within Tanimoto 0.6 of the running best, per-session top-thirty spanning as few as 2-5 generic frameworks on three objectives, up to 45% of late proposals repeating a score already seen to six decimals), and a stage that optimises every slot toward the already-fitted posterior mean reinforces that collapse by construction. Breadth has to be admitted on its own terms - diversity-aware pool admission, an explicit scaffold-level jump operator, or a ranking model whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes - and the 102 degenerate micro-molecules that still consume evaluations all come from the crossover path this stage does not touch, so a refinement attached to one origin leaves the other origin's failure mode intact.

What stays open is attribution, and the honest reading is that it is not settled by this node. The panel gain is real and it is concentrated: three of fifteen cells carry 79% of it, half of the prior path's increment mass is one session, and the largest contributor is one rare realization - only 2 of 189 previously recorded deco_hop seed-2 cells exceeded 0.70, and one of them was in this same lineage, so the basin is reachable without this mechanism. Within the field-reduced regime the ordering is consistent (no-prior control -0.0557 against the Anchor, raw-prior Parent -0.0519, this arm -0.0063) and every task mean is above both references, which is the strongest evidence the route has produced; but that ordering mixes three differences at once and the unselected raw continuations carry no counterfactual score, so it supports the joint recipe rather than the refinement stage as a component. A replication of this arm on the same code at new Confirmation-style realizations is what would separate a reproducible recovery from a lucky cell, and it is the one remaining iteration this route justifies before any change of statistic is tested; the complementary same-round arm that forces the allocator to buy raw distant chemistry answers the other half, and between them the campaign will know whether the allocator refused a good candidate or the candidate arrived off the ridge.
finding_summary.results:
The stage executed exactly as pre-registered and the audit is complete. All 17,358 admitted prior-origin pool slots across the fifteen sessions were refined (the Parent refined none of its 17,302), four variants requested every time, 68,288 of 69,432 variants admitted with every rejection carrying an inherited reason, one single slot left unrefined because all four of its variants hit the sulfur gate, and zero refinement events on graph-edit slots. It cost nothing it was not allowed to cost: no oracle call, no extra model fit, no extra covariance factorization, 435 posterior fits and 870 factorizations exactly as in the Parent, 300 oracle calls and 290 accepted proposals with zero invalid and zero duplicate proposals in every cell, full 160-member pools in all 435 batches, and the prior itself byte-identical (same three per-seed parameter hashes, frozen, no gradient update, no oracle label). Wall time rose to 1.05-2.90 times the Parent's per cell, at most 296 seconds against a two-hour task limit.

The variant chosen by the posterior replaced the raw continuation in 12,181 of 17,358 slots (70.2%, inside the registered 55-95% range), always with a non-negative posterior gain, but the gain was small: median +0.0030 in score units against a pre-registered floor of +0.005, with an upper quartile of +0.0149. The refined products kept their distance, which was the mechanism's stated risk: occupants sit at median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.6129 to their conditioning parent (Parent 0.6092; the graph-edit arm of the same sessions 0.8306), 71.3% still change three or more heavy atoms (Parent 70.3%; graph arm 30.6%), 96.4% still change the Murcko core, and the median per-slot distance change from raw to occupant is zero. Nothing collapsed into ordinary graph editing.

What the refinement bought downstream is much smaller than registered. The surrogate's pricing of the group barely moved: the prior group's median predicted score reached the graph group's in 7 of 435 batches against a pre-registered 25%, its maximum reached the graph maximum in 2 of 435 against 20%, the median in-pool predicted-score percentile of the picks it did make rose from 0.415 to 0.465 against a target of 0.50, and the uncertainty percentile stayed at 0.780 to four decimals. Purchases rose from 5.31% to 7.75% of the 4,350 evaluations, short of the registered 8% floor; 253 of 435 batches still bought no prior-origin candidate (target below 50%), though every one of the fifteen sessions now buys at least one, where the Parent had a session that bought none at all. Landing split in two directions. The quantity the question was built on moved the wrong way: the accepted median score of prior-origin products fell from 0.1853 to 0.1757, against a target of at least 0.22 and the same sessions' graph arm at 0.3112, with mean child-minus-best-parent worsening from -0.0682 to -0.0932 and the survivor rate easing from 0.675 to 0.653. Realized conversion nevertheless improved: the parent-beating rate rose from 0.108 to 0.151, prior-origin incumbent improvements from 13 to 20, sessions with at least one from 7 to 10 of 15, and the prior path's share of realized incumbent-increment mass from 2.8% to 9.1%. Because both quantities did not stay at or below the Parent's, neither registered falsifier branch fired, and neither did the distance-collapse branch or the timeout branch.

The panel rose. Paired on matched seeds against the round-42 corpus-prior arm the fifteen-cell mean is +0.0456 (seeds -0.0010 / +0.0592 / +0.0787), with ten cells up, four down and one tied, and all five task means above both the Parent and the round-43 no-prior breadth control. Against the formal Anchor the panel is -0.0063, inside the law-free ungated reference band, where the Parent sat at -0.0519; median_2 is +0.0310 above the Anchor, clear of its reference band; and of the Parent's three breached must-preserve margins only sitagliptin_mpo remains breached, at -0.0636. The deco_hop margin is held at -0.0053, the first time an ungated law-changing child of this Anchor has not paid the familiar -0.085 to -0.116 departure cost on that task - and it is held for a single reason, the seed-2 cell at 0.8713.

That cell is traceable to one event. At batch 18 of deco_hop seed 2 a prior continuation entered pool slot 111, four variants were generated, and the posterior preferred one that appended a fluorine onto a ring nitrogen already carrying a chlorine, worth +0.0035 of posterior mean. The allocator then bought that slot at the 0.396 in-pool predicted-score percentile with the 0.874 uncertainty percentile - a below-median-priced, high-uncertainty exploration draw, not a candidate the refinement had made attractive - and it scored 0.853304, beating the incumbent by +0.2552. Every one of the 103 molecules the session subsequently scored at or above 0.80 is a descendant of it, and the 0.871279 endpoint is its best descendant. Recomputed in the same pool, the unrefined continuation would have sat at percentile 0.333 instead of 0.396: the refinement moved that slot eleven ranks out of 160 and left it below the pool median. That cell alone is 37.7% of the fifteen-cell gain; with sitagliptin_mpo seed 1 and drd2_docking seed 1 it is 79%, and the other twelve cells average +0.0119.

molecular.headline: Flat halogen-decorated heterocycles, zero stereochemistry, zero charge; three sets are topped by N-F, N-Br or N-S bonds a chemist would reject.
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the node proposes mid-sized, ring-dense, strongly aromatic, achiral neutral molecules: 23-33 heavy atoms, 3.0-4.8 rings and 1.9-3.8 aromatic rings per molecule read over the 870 proposals per objective, with the digest's string counters agreeing (ring_closure_rate 0.967-0.984, aromatic_atom_rate 0.872-0.974, stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate <=0.0023 on every set). The chemistry is recognisable medicinal chemistry at the scaffold level - indole-2-carboxamides, quinazoline-purinedione biaryls, aryl-ethyl-pyrrolidine amines, benzodioxole glutarimides, N-aryl xanthines - and it is decorated by single-atom moves at the periphery. Where the molecules stop being chemistry is exactly where the score is highest: the top decile of three objectives is dominated by heteroatom-halogen bonds (N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-F), acyl fluorides, free thiols, sulfenamides, thiosulfonates and strained three-membered fused rings, because a terminal single-atom swap onto a heteroatom is the cheapest accepted move and nothing in the admission or refinement path prices it out. The new oracle-free refinement stage is visible in the molecules - 12,181 of 17,358 prior-origin slots across the 15 sessions had their decoded continuation displaced by one of four single-call variants - but it inherits the same single-atom vocabulary, so it polishes substituents and never repairs or rebuilds a ring system or installs a complete functional group. The largest single incumbent jump in the whole node (+0.2484, one session) was a refinement variant whose winning edit appended a fluorine onto an already N-chlorinated ring nitrogen.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the 15 sessions 12,181 of 17,358 refined slots replaced the raw continuation, and the winning variant was a single-atom append, replace, delete or insert in 9,830 of them against 1,998 ring-opening or ring-closing moves and 353 bond-order changes. Nothing in the refined output assembles a complete multi-atom group: sulfonyl occurs in 0.1-0.3% of three proposal sets, and where a sulfone does appear at the top of one set it is a methylsulfonyl reached atom by atom, with the thiosulfonate near-miss S(=O)(=O)S surviving into the same top decile.
transferable_gaps.gap: The refinement variants are drawn from the same single-atom vocabulary as the edit path, so refinement can only re-decorate a decoded molecule, never repair or rebuild its ring system.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A refinement stage that is meant to finish a distant proposal needs moves at a different granularity from the ones that generated the pool: attachment or exchange of whole chemically-sensible fragments from a fixed group library, and replacement of a whole ring system, so that one accepted refinement step can carry a complete functional group rather than one of its intermediates.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Refinement replacements introduced a new heteroatom-halogen bond 170 times, a new three- or four-membered ring 795 times, a new acyl halide 21 times and a new cumulated C=C=C 26 times; raw continuations already carried 2,522 strained small rings, 546 heteroatom-halogen bonds, 303 cumulated dienes and 136 acyl halides before refinement saw them. The consequences are visible at the top: 67.8% of one set's highest-scoring decile carries an N-halogen bond and 32.2% an acyl fluoride, 41.4% of another's carries an N-halogen bond, and the single highest-scoring molecule of a third carries an N-S sulfenamide on a pyrrole nitrogen.
transferable_gaps.gap: Neither the admission path nor the posterior screen rejects chemically non-viable bonds, so the refinement stage actively installs them and they propagate into the highest-scoring molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A valence-and-stability filter belongs in the shared admission path that both the edit products and the refinement variants pass through, rejecting heteroatom-halogen bonds, acyl halides, hypofluorites, peroxides, cumulated dienes and strained fused three-membered rings before a candidate can occupy a pool slot. A surrogate fitted on scored molecules cannot learn this because the objective itself does not penalise it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five proposal sets and the '@' character appears in none of the 15 trajectory files. Yet 81.0% of one set's proposals carry at least one undefined sp3 centre, another set's top decile averages 1.5 and a third's 2.1, and the ceiling-reaching molecules are 3-substituted pyrrolidines and tetrahydropyridines whose configuration is simply unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no defined stereochemistry at all, even though its own highest-scoring molecules on three of the five objectives are built on saturated ring or chain centres that are stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: No operator in the current family can set, flip or inherit a chiral tag, and the new refinement stage adds four more variants that also cannot. A task-agnostic generator needs a stereochemistry-aware proposal move - assign or invert a tetrahedral centre, set double-bond geometry - plus a canonicalization and admission path that preserve configuration, so that two enantiomers are distinguishable candidates rather than the same string.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest's charged_rate is 0.0000-0.0023 on all five sets. On the one set where a basic amine is present in 100% of the highest-scoring decile and 67.5% of the whole set, every one of those amines is written neutral, and no carboxylate, amidinium, protonated amine or quaternary nitrogen appears anywhere in the 4,350 proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: Charged and zwitterionic forms are absent from the entire output, including the regions where the rewarded feature is a centre that would be ionised.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set only ever produces neutral valence-complete atoms, so any chemistry expressed at a charged centre is approached only through its neutral surrogate. A generator should be able to propose formally charged or zwitterionic forms, and the admission and fingerprint paths should carry the charge rather than normalise it away.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 102 emitted and scored molecules across the 15 sessions have six or fewer heavy atoms - C, C#C, COC, CC, ClBr, FBr, C=COOC=C, N#CCS, C=C(C)Br, Cc1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 - and all 102 were produced with crossover as the requested operator on the graph-edit side; none came from a prior-origin slot, refined or raw. Most score zero or near zero, and they occur as late as evaluation 299.
transferable_gaps.gap: Degenerate micro-molecules still consume oracle evaluations, and every one of them comes from the crossover path that the new refinement stage does not cover.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A refinement or screening stage attached to one proposal origin leaves the other origin's failure mode untouched. A heavy-atom floor tied to the size of the conditioning parents, enforced in the shared admission path for every origin, would convert those evaluations into usable proposals; two parents whose connected-fragment recombination can return a two-atom product need that product rejected before it is priced.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over evaluations 201-300, between 9% and 58% of proposals sit within Morgan Tanimoto 0.6 of the running best molecule, and per-session highest-scoring thirty molecules span as few as 2-5 generic frameworks on three of the five objectives. Up to 45% of late proposals repeat a score already seen to six decimals, and one set shows nine molecules within 0.014 of each other that differ only by permuting methyl, methoxy and thiomethyl around the same ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late search collapses onto one decorated framework and re-prices it one atom at a time, and the added refinement stage does not widen it.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Parent selection plus single-atom edits turns the back half of every budget into local re-pricing of one framework, and a refinement stage that optimises each slot toward the already-fitted posterior mean reinforces that by construction, since the posterior is highest near what has already scored well. Breadth has to be admitted on its own terms - diversity-aware pool admission, an explicit scaffold-level jump operator, or a refinement objective that is not the same mean the selector maximises.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Prior-origin molecules remain the minority of accepted proposals (1-26 raw and 2-30 refined per session out of 290) and their accepted means stay below the graph-edit group on 14 of the 15 sessions. The one case where a prior-origin molecule carried a large incumbent jump is instructive about what the screen rewards: the winning variant of that slot differed from its decoded continuation by appending a halogen onto a ring nitrogen that already bore a chlorine, giving Cn1c(=O)n(C=O)c(=O)c2c(N(F)Cl)n(-c3ncnc4cc(OC(F)(F)F)c(Cl)cc34)c(Br)c21.
transferable_gaps.gap: Screening variants by posterior mean selects for proximity to already-scored chemistry, so the distant proposals the prior supplies are pulled back toward the incumbent rather than finished.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A screen whose statistic is the mean of a surrogate fitted on the incumbent population will prefer the variant that most resembles what already scored, which is the opposite of what finishing a distant proposal requires. If distant chemistry is to be refined rather than domesticated, the variant choice needs a statistic that admits predicted improvement or uncertainty, or a chemically-motivated acceptance rule independent of the surrogate, and the variants themselves need to be able to complete a structure rather than decorate it.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
